tool.name: PyEuk process-ONT
tool.description: call amplicon haplotypes from Oxford Nanopore reads
tool.command: pyeuk process-ont --input-fastq '$input_fastq' --sample-id '$sample_id' #if $reference_fasta --reference-fasta '$reference_fasta' #end if #if $de_novo --de-novo #end if --qscore $qscore --output-dir out && ## process-ont writes the calls to <output-dir>/<sample-id> (no extension). cp out/'$sample_id' '$calls'

param.label: Sample identifier
param.help: Specimen id; becomes the id in the output.

param.label: Reference MLST FASTA (optional)
param.help: Reference MLST FASTA. Omit and tick de novo to discover consensus haplotypes from the reads.

param.label: De novo consensus discovery
param.help: Build consensus haplotypes from the reads with no reference database.

param.label: Minimum mean read Q-score
param.help: Minimum mean read quality. Raise it to trade yield for accuracy.

tool.help:
Types one specimen from Oxford Nanopore amplicon reads. A long ONT read spans a whole amplicon in one molecule, so a haplotype is read straight off a single read.
The tool filters reads by mean quality (``qscore``), aligns them to a reference marker FASTA (or, with de novo, builds a consensus per amplicon with no reference), and writes per-specimen haplotype calls in the same format as the Illumina caller, ready for Build haplotype sheet.
Give either a reference FASTA or tick de novo. Raise the Q-score to trade yield for accuracy on a noisy run. @HELP_FOOTER@
